source.extractionNote: Geometry read over the 9 Size x Shape variants at primary/default; colour over the 55 Flavour x State/Disabled variants at small/rounded; every other variant scanned for colour consistency (2 mismatches, in issues). Intent verbatim from the 2026-10-29 spec.

summary: Triggers an action from a text label, with optional icons on either side. Eleven flavours set how much weight the action carries, three sizes and three shapes fit it to the surface it sits on. The label is the only content a consumer writes, everything else is a variant choice. When an action has no text label, use Icon Button rather than hiding this one's label.

intent.primary: The single most important action in a view, one per group. If two buttons both read as primary, the view has two competing goals and that is a layout problem rather than a property one.
intent.positive: Confirms a constructive outcome such as approving or publishing. Reserve it for the confirmation itself, not for every agreeable action, or it stops signalling anything.
intent.negative: Destructive actions the user cannot undo, such as delete or revoke. If the cancel beside it is styled any stronger than subtle, the safe choice becomes the harder one to find.
intent.subtle: A neutral action meant to sit quietly beside a stronger one, typically the cancel next to a primary. It leans on that neighbour for contrast, so on its own it may not read as interactive.
intent.text: A tertiary action inside dense content. It has nothing behind it at rest, so on a coloured or busy surface it stops looking like a control.
intent.outline-subtle: A secondary action on a busy surface where an accent border would compete. It reads as neutral, so it is the wrong choice for the main action on that surface.
intent.outline: A secondary action that still needs to look clickable on its own. Two of them side by side read as equal weight, which is rarely what was intended.
intent.gradient: One promotional or high-emphasis moment, such as an upgrade prompt. It outranks primary, so a screen carrying two of them has no hierarchy left.
intent.text-gradient: The promotional treatment without the filled weight, for a high-emphasis action inside content. The gradient runs across the label itself, so a very short label barely shows it.
intent.contrast: The strongest neutral against the page, near-black in light mode and near-white in dark. Beside a primary it competes for weight, so pair it with outline or text instead.
intent.outline-contrast: A secondary action that pairs with contrast. Its border and label follow the page, near-black in light mode and near-white in dark.

size.orderedBy: rootWidth (small 76 < medium 90 < large 98); Figma stores the options in creation order
size.note: Adopted in code 2026-11-07; the metadata still calls small the default — see issues.

intent.small: The default, for toolbars, table rows and dense forms where controls sit close together.
intent.medium: For standard forms and dialogs where the button is a deliberate step rather than a dense control.
intent.large: For a call to action that should be easy to hit without precision, typically the confirm on a touch surface.

intent.sharp: Match the container. Correct when the surrounding surface and inputs are square.
intent.rounded: Match the container. The general-purpose choice alongside the system's other rounded controls.
intent.full: A deliberately soft treatment for standalone or promotional actions. Beside rounded controls in the same group it looks unintentional.

state.note: Documentation-only in Figma. In code these are interaction states the implementation drives, not a prop a consumer sets.

intent.default: The resting state, and the only one to use when laying out a static screen.
intent.hover: Documents the pointer-over treatment. The implementation drives this, so choosing it in a layout freezes the button in a state it should not be in.
intent.pressed: Documents the pointer-down treatment, with the same caveat as hover.
intent.focus: Documents the keyboard focus treatment. The one state whose treatment is identical on every flavour.

disabled.note: Modelled as a VARIANT axis in Figma, but boolean in nature; implement as a boolean prop. Only the combination State=default + Disabled=true exists, so there is no hover/pressed/focus treatment for a disabled button by design.

intent.true: The action is unavailable. Say why somewhere nearby, because a disabled control with no explanation is indistinguishable from a broken one.

intent.text: The action the user is about to perform, written as a verb. The button hugs whatever it is given, so a long label widens the control and can break a toolbar row.

intent.true: Adds an icon before the label to reinforce the action at a glance. Choose the glyph deliberately, the slot arrives holding a default that suits almost nothing.
Turning both icons on at small leaves very little room for the label itself. Use a trailing icon for directional or disclosure actions.

internalVariations.options: any glyph in the icon library
internalVariations.intent: Any glyph from the icon library. Both slots arrive holding Verified, which suits almost no real action, so set it deliberately whenever a slot is turned on.
internalVariations.decision: Button does not re-declare this as its own property. Whether it becomes a prop (e.g. leadingIcon: <glyph>) in code is the implementer's call.

internalVariations.property: Size, Framed (VARIANT on the nested Icon)
internalVariations.intent: Button does not re-declare Icon's other properties, but the instance stays exposed, so Icon's glyph, Size and Framed are still reachable in the properties panel. See the Icon Metadata frame for what Icon itself offers, and leave its Size alone, Button pairs it to the label.
internalVariations.decision: Button pins Size per its own Size (small -> Icon small, medium/large -> Icon medium) and Framed=false. Do not expose these.

anatomy.role: The button's own horizontal auto-layout frame. Carries the background, the border and the radius, and holds the height fixed for the chosen Size.

paint.stroke: per flavour x state, inside at rest; focus outside

anatomy.role: An Icon instance before the label, hidden until Leading Icon is turned on. Button sets its size and leaves the instance exposed.

fill.token: per flavour, following the label (overridden on the instance)
fill.boundInside: Icon binds foreground/primary; Button overrides it in every flavour and in disabled

anatomy.role: A wrapper frame around the text. Its own horizontal padding is what separates the text from the icons, the row itself has no gap.
An Icon instance after the label, hidden until Trailing Icon is turned on.

fill.token: per flavour, following the label (overridden on the instance)

bySize._note: Every cell is a token name except the two suffixed Px, which are measurements. The icon is sized by the nested Icon's Size variant, which Button pins (small -> Icon small, medium and large -> Icon medium).

byFlavourState._note: Identical at every size and shape except the two mismatches in issues. Border weights: stroke/base draws nothing (0px, see issues), stroke/thin draws 1px inside, stroke/thick draws 2px outside. Scrim rows carry Figma's extra paint opacity (@ n), which doubles the token's own alpha — code binds the token alone (see issues).

subcomponents.name: Icon
subcomponents.where: local, on the Icon page (not the Button page)
subcomponents.note: Button uses only its small and medium steps, always Framed=false. Its glyph vector binds foreground/primary; Button overrides the fill per flavour.

subcomponents.name: Icon Button
subcomponents.note: Shares the Button page and has its own metadata frame, but it is a sibling public component, not a subcomponent.

tokens.color: the six interactive/* families (primary, positive, destructive, neutral, ghost, inverse), each with background, border and foreground sub-groups across default/hover/pressed/focused/disabled; plus interactive/secondary/border/disabled, border/focus, border/disabled, surface/gradient/{start,end}, foreground/gradient/{start,end} and foreground/primary
tokens.effects: none — no shadows, no elevation, anywhere in the component

themeAxes._note: palette is the only axis that changes Button; every dimension and typography token resolves identically across the size and typography modes.

states.change: Background, border and label sit on the default tokens of the chosen flavour.

Filled flavours move their own background token one step. Outline flavours hold their border and shift a neutral background underneath instead. Text flavours raise a ghost scrim from fully transparent. The gradient flavours keep their gradient and slide it toward the end colour rather than swapping it (see Gradient transition). outline-contrast steps its border and raises the ghost scrim. Apart from text-gradient, the label colour does not change on any flavour.
The same mechanism as hover carried one step further. The gradient flavours slide the other way, toward the start colour, rather than collapsing to a flat token (see Gradient transition).
A focus ring is drawn outside the bounds, replacing the resting border rather than adding to it. Identical on all eleven flavours, and the only state that changes the control's outer footprint.
Background and label swap to the disabled tokens of their family, and the icon follows the label. No flavour keeps its accent colour, so disabled buttons of different flavours look alike.

behavior.description: Figma stores no timing. Every state change is colour-only, with no scale, shadow or elevation shift on any flavour, so a transition should read as a tint change rather than movement. The gradient flavours are the one exception to a plain tint: their gradient moves (see Gradient transition).

gradient and text-gradient keep their gradient through every state and move it rather than replace it. On hover the gradient slides until its end colour covers 100% of the fill (the label's own text on text-gradient); on press it slides the other way until its start colour covers 100%. Leaving or releasing slides it back to the resting two-stop gradient. It must never jump from the gradient to a flat colour: a browser cannot interpolate between a gradient and a solid fill, so that swap shows as a flicker. The hover and pressed variants show where each slide ends, not a separate flat fill.
The only change that alters the control's outer footprint, because the ring is drawn outside the bounds. Leave room around a button in a tight row so the ring is not clipped.
The control re-hugs its label whenever the text changes, so a label swapped at runtime shifts the position of everything beside it in a row.
outline-contrast takes its border from interactive/inverse/border/* and its label from foreground/primary, so it follows the mode. Its states sit on interactive/ghost/background/*.

content.description: A verb phrase naming the action. The button hugs whatever length it is given, there is no truncation and no wrapping.

Toggles visibility only. Button does not re-declare Icon's other properties, but the instance stays exposed, so Icon's glyph, Size and Framed are still reachable in the properties panel. See the Icon Metadata frame for what Icon itself offers, and leave its Size alone, Button pairs it to the label.
The same slot mechanics as Leading Icon, placed after the label instead.

content.type: instance swap on the nested Icon
content.description: Any glyph from the icon library. Both slots arrive holding Verified, which suits almost no real action, so set it deliberately whenever a slot is turned on.

do: Use one primary per view or per group. Everything else steps down to outline, subtle or text so the single most important action stays findable.
Write the label as the verb the user is about to perform, Save rather than OK, so the action still reads clearly on its own.
dont: Don't build an icon-only button by hiding this one's label. Icon Button is a separate square component made for that, and it keeps the touch target correct.
Don't mix Shape values inside one button group. A pill beside a rounded button reads as a mistake rather than a deliberate distinction.

accessibility: Focus is drawn as a ring outside the control and is identical on every flavour, so it stays visible whatever the button sits on.
Disabled is a visual state only. Figma cannot carry the reason an action is unavailable, so put that in nearby text in the implementation.
The icon repeats the label rather than adding to it. An action with no visible label belongs in Icon Button, which still needs an accessible name in code.
Every state change is colour-only, so anything signalled by hover or pressed alone will not reach a keyboard or screen reader user.
Write labels as the verb the user is about to carry out, Save rather than OK, so the action is understandable when read out of context.

layoutTheming.description: Always hugs the label and any visible icons, never fixed. Small grows by 16px for each icon shown, medium and large by 20px.
control/sm at small, control/md at medium, control/lg at large. Not resizable independently of Size.
space/md at small and medium, space/lg at large.
space/2xs at every size. The fixed height does the real work.
Item spacing is space/none. The visible separation between an icon and the label comes from the Label wrapper's own horizontal padding, space/2xs at small and space/sm at medium and large.
radius/none for sharp, radius/element-sm for rounded, radius/pill for full. All three are token-bound, so match the container rather than overriding on the instance.
1px drawn inside on outline, outline-subtle and outline-contrast, none on the other eight at rest. Focus replaces it with a 2px ring drawn outside the bounds.
16px at small, 20px at medium and large. Large reuses Icon's medium step, so Icon's own large (28px) never appears inside a Button.
label/medium at small, label/large at medium and large.

Every fill, border and label colour is bound to an interactive/* token for the flavour. Gradient draws from surface/gradient/*, text-gradient from foreground/gradient/*, contrast from interactive/inverse/*, outline-contrast from interactive/inverse/border/* and foreground/primary, and focus from border/focus. No variant hardcodes a colour.

issues.detail: The set's defaults moved to medium/rounded in Figma and code adopted them (react-baseui and zds; zeta-web already defaulted so) — a breaking default change. The metadata's size intent still calls small the default; update the frame.

The nested icons are hidden by default and a hidden instance exposes no layers to a read-only extraction, so the per-flavour fill override on the icon instances cannot be verified read-only. Icon Button, whose glyph is visible, binds it to the flavour's foreground token; expect the same here and confirm by turning an icon on before relying on it.

The scrim flavours (text, text-gradient, subtle, outline-subtle) set a paint-level opacity of 0 / 0.05 / 0.10 on interactive/ghost/background/*. Those tokens already carry the scrim in their own alpha, so Figma applies it twice: the hover scrim renders at about 0.25% and pressed at 1%, practically invisible. Code binds the tokens directly with no paint opacity (the intended 5% / 10%); the Figma paints should drop their opacity to 1.

stroke/base resolves to 0px although its description reads '= 1px, source: scale/0'. It is the border width on the eight non-outline flavours, so those carry a fully bound but zero-width border. A rebuild that trusts the token name or description will draw a 1px border where Figma draws none.

Seven dimension tokens have descriptions that state the wrong px value: control/sm says 40 -> resolves 36; control/md says 48 -> 40; control/lg says 56 -> 48; space/none says 32 -> 0; radius/element-sm says 16 -> 4; radius/none says 2 -> 0; stroke/base says 1 -> 0. The resolved values match the metadata's Layout & Theming table, so build from those.

positive + disabled borrows another family's token: its border is interactive/secondary/border/disabled while every other flavour uses its own family's disabled border. Everything resolves to line/subtle, so nothing looks wrong, but the binding is inconsistent.

The metadata's hover grouping is out of date: it says outline flavours shift a neutral background and text flavours raise the ghost scrim. In the file outline-subtle and subtle raise the ghost scrim like text; only outline shifts a neutral background.

gradient + pressed at Size=small, Shape=sharp takes its border from border/gradient/start; the other eight size/shape variants use interactive/primary/border/pressed. Invisible today (stroke/base), but it is the only place border/gradient/start appears on Button.

outline + disabled at Size=large, Shape=full draws interactive/ghost/background/disabled @ 0 with interactive/ghost/foreground/disabled; the other eight size/shape variants draw interactive/neutral/background/disabled with interactive/neutral/foreground/disabled.

contrast and outline-contrast were cloned from primary and outline; their hidden icon instances cannot be read, so the fills override likely still carries primary's and outline's icon colour. Code is unaffected: the glyph takes currentColor.

The gradient variants agree with the intended transition: hover binds surface/gradient/end and pressed surface/gradient/start (text-gradient: foreground/gradient/*). Each variant shows where its slide ends. Focus also binds the start colour; the metadata gives focus only the ring, so code keeps the resting gradient at focus.

Disabled is a two-option VARIANT axis rather than a Figma boolean, and State is documentation-only. In code, disabled is a boolean and hover/pressed/focus are interaction states. Only State=default pairs with Disabled=true.

Figma returns VARIANT options in creation order — Size as [medium, large, small], Shape as [rounded, sharp, full], Flavour as [primary, positive, negative, outline, outline-subtle, text, subtle, gradient, text-gradient, contrast, outline-contrast]. The metadata's order is the order to ship.
The icon glyph is an INSTANCE_SWAP on the nested Icon, not a Button property, and Icon's Size/Framed stay reachable on the exposed instance. Button pins them; do not expose Size or Framed.

Icon (2046:15010) is local but on the Icon page, and its default glyph (Verified -> Style=rounded) is on the Assets page. Neither is remote; neither is on the Button page. Icon Button (2338:1763) is a sibling public set sharing the page, specced separately.

Motion is intentionally not modelled ('Figma stores no timing'), there are no effect styles or shadows, and no variant hardcodes a colour: the full scan found zero untokenised visual values; binding drift is limited to the two variants above. palette is the only theme axis that changes Button.
